claims.statement: All four workflows run on GitHub-hosted `ubuntu-latest` runners with one concurrency group per PR: tests on PRs to dev/main, compose-boot on PRs plus pushes to dev, secrets on PRs plus pushes to dev, backmerge on pushes to main.

tests.yml runs npm ci --ignore-scripts (rebuilding better-sqlite3 and argon2 explicitly), then audit:gate, lint, build, typecheck, arch:check and test:coverage against a throwaway postgres:17-alpine container; audit:gate fails on unlisted advisories, entries npm audit no longer reports, and expired reviewBy dates.

compose-boot.yml builds and boots the real compose stack: it generates a throwaway env file with every variable required at boot, creates the bind-mount apps/*/data directories chowned to 1000:1000, asserts each backend's /health/ready from inside its own container, and always tears down with `down -v`.

secrets.yml scans every commit (fetch-depth 0) with gitleaks in a digest-pinned read-only image using --redact; .gitleaks.toml allowlists exactly one path (packages/crypto/test/envelope.test.ts, a published NIST vector), and npm run secrets runs the same scan locally.

backmerge.yml opens a `-s ours` bookkeeping PR on every push to main so main stays an ancestor of dev after a squash promotion; it must be merged with a merge commit and requires the repo setting that allows Actions to create pull requests.

RULE 7 in scripts/arch-check.mjs fails when any workflow file names `self-hosted` (comments stripped, any trigger), and the repository's only self-hosted runner (fedora-sonarqube) was unregistered when the repo went public — the live count must stay 0.
